subject: StellarFlow load-run handoff: scripts, allowlist, and test window
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.run>
To: Alex Ramos <alex.ramos@stellarflow.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: load-run targets & next steps

Hi Alex — thanks again for the demo time this morning. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we can get the customer-led load run scheduled and unblocked: 

SLOs / targets you asked us to validate:
- 95th-pct generation latency <= 350ms (128-token generation)
- Sustained throughput: 40 req/s (text generation)
- Concurrent open streams: 80 simultaneous streaming connections
- Streaming chunk latency (RTT for token chunks) < 150ms

What we need from you to proceed:
1) Test account(s): email + token we can use for k6/Locust to hit your app endpoint (or confirm we should call your public API directly).
2) IP allowlist: list of client IPs we should permit (we'll provide Redwood egress IPs).
3) Test window: propose Tue Jul 7, 09:00–11:00 PT (we can adapt).
4) Which flow to test: server-side streaming (chunked responses) or client-side chunking? If both, we should break into two waves.

Attachments: I attached the initial k6 scenario (stellarflow_k6_scenario_v1.js) and a short README with data generation notes. The script is intentionally conservative on ramp to reduce risk; Ben can uplift the ramping and concurrency knobs during the run.

Next steps (owner):
- Alex: confirm test account + allowlist + internal ops contact (by EOB today would be great)
- Redwood (Soojin): validate account and provision test tokens; handoff to engineering for script tuning
- Redwood (Ben): standby to update script and watch the run; provide fallback (lower-concurrency) plan if capacity is constrained

Thanks — I’ll queue a preflight checklist 48 hours before the window.

— Soojin
Soojin Lee
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.run

Thanks Soojin — this is great and matches what we need to validate. Quick answers: 

- Test account: create test-k6@stellarflow.com and issue an API token with read/write limited scope; OK to share creds over a signed DocuSign link or secure portal.
- Allowlist: our infra team can add Redwood egress IPs; their contact is ops@stellarflow.com. The public IPs we see from your demo session were 34.201.33.44 and 18.204.12.10 — please confirm these are the egress addresses for the run or provide updated list.
- Waves: yes — please do two waves: wave A server-streaming (50 concurrent) and wave B full-concurrency (80 concurrent) to validate degradation curves.
- Test window: Jul 7 09:00–11:00 PT works for us. We'll have two SREs on call.

Also, can you confirm expected payload sizes? Most of our streaming tests are 64–128 tokens.

Alex Ramos
CTO, StellarFlow

- Customer provided ops contact (ops@stellarflow.com) and two public IPs; ask them to add our egress list.

- Upload the k6 script to the shared Drive (or repo) and send back the exact path we should run from the execution hosts.
- Provide a temporary test token for the customer endpoint or instruct ops on token creation flow.
- Confirm the Redwood egress IP block we need whitelisted.

I'll track scheduling and preflight. If either of you prefer a short 20-minute pre-run sync (Fri Jul 5), say the word.

— Soojin

Thanks — picking this up. Details below and actionables I completed: 

1) Script location: uploaded a tuned k6 scenario to Drive: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1aBcDk-example-script (same as link in metadata). File: stellarflow_k6_scenario_v1.js. The script includes two scenarios (server_stream_wave and full_concurrency_wave) with configurable ENV vars: TARGET_URL, API_TOKEN, CONCURRENCY, RAMP_DURATION.

2) Test creds: I created a scoped token for test-k6@stellarflow.com. We'll share the token via our secure vault (I will generate a one-time access link and send to Alex via ops@stellarflow.com).

3) IP allowlist: Redwood egress for the run will come from the following CIDR blocks: 34.201.33.0/24 and 18.204.12.0/24. Alex — confirm these map to the IPs you saw and ask your infra to whitelist the /24 blocks for the window.

4) Streaming guidance: For server-streaming wave A, set CONCURRENCY=50 and chunk_wait=50ms in the script. For wave B (stress), set CONCURRENCY=80, ramp 5 minutes to target. If you need to validate lower-latency streaming chunk RTT, we can add a micro-benchmark that measures first-chunk time separately.

5) Fallback plan: if we hit capacity limits on Redwood Dedicated for the exact model you picked, we'll automatically fall back to a lighter quantized variant (same family) and re-run wave B at 60 concurrency to validate functional SLOs — we will flag this in the post-run report.

Attachments: pushed updated script (stellarflow_k6_scenario_v1.js) and the README explaining sample data generation (loadtest_data_readme.pdf).

I can be on call for the run and watch the runtime dashboards; planning to allocate Ben Carter (engineer) + one runtime on-call. If Marissa wants to coordinate logistics and escalation, LMK.

— Ben
